blockCoverage.observation: Fixed suspension, inextensible negligible-mass string, point-mass bob and taut-string condition are retained before the motion description. Length is defined to the center of mass and identified with string length only within this model. The signed angle convention is explicit in both directions. Speed change, tangential acceleration and the contrast with radial acceleration are not conflated. Paragraph 1's 'In this model' refers intelligibly to paragraph 0.

Rightward tangential positive direction and restoring sign are retained. G_tau=-G sin(alpha)=-mg sin(alpha), ma_tau=G_tau and equation (1.6) keep their meanings and labels. The final saved paragraph explicitly limits a_tau to a projection rather than the entire acceleration vector. Formula introduction, sign interpretation and Newton-law step remain readable in order.

Division by mass gives a_tau=-g sin(alpha), labelled (1.7); mass cancellation is qualified by the stated ideal conditions. This paragraph closes the non-small-angle relation before the next concept boundary.

The exact sine relation is distinguished from the later approximation, without dropping the taut-string condition. Small angular displacement throughout the swing and radians precede sin(alpha) approximately alpha and (1.8). The equality notation in the approximate equation is explicitly qualified in prose; larger angles are excluded. Each saved paragraph has a clear role and the warning follows the approximation.

OA precedes signed arc length s in the corrected sentence. Equilibrium O and the right/left signs are retained, followed by radian-conditioned s=alpha l, (1.9). The arc-versus-chord distinction is intact. Figure 6 is only the retained textual source reference; no attachment is required or authorized by this review.

Substitution alpha=s/l is explicitly in the small-angle equation and preserves a_tau=-(g/l)s, (1.10). Direction toward equilibrium and magnitude proportional to arc-distance are kept separate. Units remain consistent with length l and s and gravitational acceleration g; no degree substitution or radial-acceleration claim is introduced.

The analogy is the same approximate equation form: a_x becomes a_tau and x becomes signed arc length s. The coefficient depends on local gravitational acceleration and pendulum length. The final paragraph retains opposite direction as well as proportional magnitude.

Different force origins are preserved. Hooke's law, small pendulum angles and negligible resistance qualify the common time-dependence type. The saved continuation explicitly rejects equal periods, amplitudes or initial states as a necessary consequence. It remains natural English and does not overstate the Chinese proposition.

Equations (1.4) and (1.10) relate acceleration and displacement; finding position versus time additionally needs solving the motion equation and knowing initial position and velocity. Neither initial condition is omitted.

Constant acceleration is contrasted with the varying restoring force and acceleration of this oscillation. The restriction on directly applying uniform-acceleration formulas to the whole oscillation is preserved. The last saved paragraph supplies a complete conclusion.
